correctness.rationale: For any partition block, the distance from a vertex in partite class A_i is exactly 0 to its own block, 2 to other blocks wholly inside A_i, and 1 to every block meeting another graph part. Hence within A_i only two representation types can occur. A resolving partition would force every graph part to have size at most two; a 2-part must have one pure singleton vertex and one mixed-block vertex, while a singleton part also has a vertex with zero 2-entries. Thus every graph part contributes the same {0,1,...,1} representation, and two graph parts force a collision. The standalone exhaustive checker independently verifies the formula and nonexistence for every complete multipartite profile through order 7.

value.rationale: The parameter was introduced in July 2026 and its initiating paper explicitly develops finite and infinite graph classes. Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical test family for any metric-partition invariant. Showing that every noncomplete member has infinite value is a natural complete classification, extends the paper’s complete-graph obstruction to all bicliques and higher multipartite graphs, and exposes a strong failure of multiset partition resolvability on one of the most basic dense graph families.
